expected_survivors.collect-boundary decodes headers against: Redundantly covered, not equivalent. decode_*_header asserts context_slot >= min_context_slot; with min_context_slot = cutoff_slot = the interval's high, that is the SAME inequality as the condition-1 check in intervals_from_boundary_evidence (high <= context_slot). On the covered branch -- the only one the fixtures reach -- reverting this floor to CUTOFF_SLOT still refuses via condition-1, which CoveredIntervalMayNotOutrunTheEvidenceTests kills directly. The floor is defence-in-depth that also guards the uncovered branch and fails earlier; its independent scenario (uncovered branch with a stale read) is not exercised by any current fixture, so it is declared here rather than killed. If a future uncovered-branch test is added this mutant should start dying, and the sweep will say so.
